_comment: Which VAPI file the voice fleet's knowledge base actually IS.
The corpus is built by build-knowledge-doc.mjs and uploaded to VAPI, where
every assistant's inline `query` tool points at it by file id. Before this
file existed that id was recorded nowhere: the document the live agents
answered from could not be compared with the repository, and re-pointing
twelve assistants was a hand step with no record that it had been done.
`sha256` is of the committed Markdown AS UPLOADED. When it stops matching
the committed file, the live agents are answering from an older corpus -
which is a different failure from the file id being wrong, and sends you
to a different remedy, so both are recorded.
UPLOAD IT AS text/plain WITH A .txt NAME. VAPI's file store accepts a
text/markdown upload, stores it byte for byte, and then marks it
status=failed with no parsed text - measured 23 Sep 2026 on two uploads
(0af91eda..., which the fleet pointed at for five hours, and a second copy
of this corpus). A failed file is bound to a query tool exactly like a good
one and nothing reports it; the agents simply have nothing to retrieve. The
same bytes uploaded as text/plain parse to status=done. So the upload is
judged by the store's own `status`, never by the upload's HTTP 201, and
`status` below is what the store said after the upload - not what was sent.
A null file_id means the fleet's knowledge base is not managed from here
and apply-fleet-upgrade.py leaves every query tool exactly as it found it.
`previous_file_id` is the last corpus that PARSED - the one to roll back to.
It is kept rather than deleted, because rolling back is then one value here
plus a re-run of apply-fleet-upgrade.py rather than a re-upload. The
Markdown file in between (0af91eda...) never parsed and is not a rollback.
